rows.evidence: Q1: Methods 2.1-2.3 - two-year (2014-15, 2015-16) replicated field experiment at BISA Ladhowal, silt loam, RCBD with four replications, eight tillage/residue/irrigation treatments. Q2: Abstract and Section 3.3, Figs 4-5 - irrigation water applied through drip (measured with water meter) was 53.0/43.2% (2014) and 47.6/42.5% (2015) lower in rice than CT-FI and ZT-FI, and 41.9/40.3% (2014-15) and 52.6/58.1% (2015-16) lower in wheat; abstract summarises savings of 48-53% in rice and 42-53% in wheat under SSDF+CA versus flood. Q8: Section 3.3 end - authors note that complete water balance components were not computed and further studies are suggested to report real water savings; Section 3.2 end - results need evaluation under different soil types, climatic conditions and irrigation availability for wider application; Conclusions - single N rate and fixed 7-day fertigation schedule used.
rows.notes: Water saving is measured only as applied irrigation volume (water meter), one method, so no triangulation. Evaporation, drainage and seepage (the loss pathways through which SSDF saves water) are not measured, only asserted/cited (Ayars et al., Sharda et al.). Single site, single soil, two crops in one rotation, plot scale (70 m2). Residue mulch increased savings but is reported as a variation, not stated as a requirement. Only LSD values/letter groupings reported; no SD, SE or CI for irrigation amounts (all replicates of a treatment received identical irrigation).

rows.evidence: Q1: Methods 2.1-2.3 - two-year replicated field experiment on SSDF under CA in rice-wheat, silt loam, NW India.
rows.notes: The study does not measure resilience, risk reduction, yield stability or any risk-management outcome. It reports irrigation water input, grain yield, irrigation water productivity, partial factor productivity of N and net returns over two seasons. Statements that SSDF is 'a potential option for a water-scarce future' and contributes to sustainable intensification (Sections 3.6, 4) are discussion/extrapolation, not an own result on resilience. The measured water savings are at most a precondition for the claimed contribution to resilient systems, hence upstream.

notes: Full text available; Table 1 is garbled by column-wise OCR but treatment details are also given in the running text. Study is a plot-scale (70 m2 plots) two-year experiment at a single site; results given as treatment means with LSD/letter groupings only.
